title: 1 John Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 John chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 John Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 John Chapter 2.

questions.question: In 1 John 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not.
He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar.
He that loveth his brother abideth in the light.
Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you.
questions.correctAnswer: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not.
questions.explanation: This statement is found in 1 John 2:1, making it the first occurrence in the chapter.

questions.question: Who is our advocate with the Father according to 1 John 2?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:1 states that 'we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.'

questions.question: What is Jesus referred to as in relation to our sins?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:2 identifies Jesus as 'the propitiation for our sins.'

questions.question: How do we know that we know Him?
options: If we read the Bible often
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:3 states, 'hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.'

questions.question: What does it mean if someone says, 'I know him,' but does not keep his commandments?
questions.explanation: According to 1 John 2:4, 'He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar.'

questions.question: What is perfected in those who keep His word?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:5 states that 'in him verily is the love of God perfected' when one keeps His word.

questions.question: How should one who abides in Him walk?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:6 says, 'He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.'

questions.question: Is the commandment that John writes a new one?
options: Yes, it is from the prophets
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:7 states, 'I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning.'

questions.question: What is true in Him and in you according to 1 John 2?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:8 mentions that the new commandment is 'true in him and in you.'

questions.question: What happens to someone who says he is in the light but hates his brother?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:9 states, 'He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.'

questions.question: What does he who loves his brother abide in?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:10 affirms that 'He that loveth his brother abideth in the light.'

questions.question: Is it true that if we sin, we have an advocate with the Father?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:1 confirms that 'if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father.'

questions.question: Is it true that keeping His commandments is a sign of knowing Him?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:3 states that knowing Him is conditional upon keeping His commandments.

questions.question: Is it false that loving one's brother leads to darkness?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:10 indicates that loving one's brother leads to abiding in the light, not darkness.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus is the propitiation only for the sins of a few?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:2 states that He is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, not just a few.

medium.title: 1 John Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 John Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 John 2:15, what happens if anyone loves the world and the things in it?
options: The love of the Father is not in him
He will have peace and joy
He will be blessed by God
questions.correctAnswer: The love of the Father is not in him
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:15 clearly states that if any man loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

questions.question: What does 1 John 2:17 promise will happen if someone does the will of God as commanded in 1 John 2:16?
options: He will be rejected by the world
He will overcome the wicked one
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:17 promises that he who does the will of God abides forever, following the command in 2:16 to reject worldly lusts.

questions.question: What is said about those who hate their brother according to 1 John 2:11?
options: They are in darkness and walk in darkness
They are forgiven for his name's sake
They have overcome the wicked one
questions.correctAnswer: They are in darkness and walk in darkness
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:11 states that he who hateth his brother is in darkness, walketh in darkness, and is blind to where he goes.

questions.question: How are the 'little children' described in both 1 John 2:12 and 1 John 2:13?
options: Their sins are forgiven and they have known the Father
They have overcome the wicked one and are strong
They have an unction from the Holy One
questions.correctAnswer: Their sins are forgiven and they have known the Father
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:12 states little children's sins are forgiven, and 2:13 says little children have known the Father.

questions.question: According to 1 John 2:18, what indicates that it is the last time?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:18 states that the presence of many antichrists is the sign that it is the last time.

questions.question: What is the reason given in 1 John 2:19 for why some went out from the community?
options: They were not truly of us
They were forgiven for their sins
They were strong and overcame the wicked one
questions.correctAnswer: They were not truly of us
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:19 explains that those who went out were not truly of the community because if they were, they would have continued with them.

questions.question: What does 1 John 2:20 say believers have received from the Holy One?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:20 states believers have an unction from the Holy One which enables them to know all things.

questions.question: What does 1 John 2:13 say about the young men?
options: They have overcome the wicked one
They have an unction from the Holy One
questions.correctAnswer: They have overcome the wicked one
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:13 states that young men have overcome the wicked one.

questions.question: According to 1 John 2:14, why are the young men described as strong?
options: Because the word of God abideth in them
questions.correctAnswer: Because the word of God abideth in them
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:14 explains that young men are strong because the word of God abides in them.

questions.question: What are the three things described in 1 John 2:16 that are 'not of the Father'?
options: The lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
questions.correctAnswer: The lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:16 lists these three as being of the world and not of the Father.

questions.question: What does 1 John 2:10 say about the one who loves his brother?
options: He abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him
He is in darkness and walks in darkness
He is overcome by the wicked one
questions.correctAnswer: He abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:10 clearly states that he who loves his brother abides in the light with no occasion to stumble.

questions.question: According to 1 John 2:3-4, how do we know we know Him?
options: If we overcome the wicked one
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:3-4 teaches that knowing Him is evidenced by keeping His commandments.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 John 2:17, the world and its lust pass away, but whoever does the will of God abides forever.
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:17 teaches that the world and its lust pass away, but the one who does God's will abides forever.

questions.question: True or False: 1 John 2:19 states that those who left the community were truly of us and would have continued with us.
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:19 states the opposite—that those who left were not truly of us, for if they had been, they would have remained.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 John 2:11, he that hates his brother is walking in the light and knows where he is going.
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:11 states that he who hates his brother is in darkness, walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going.

hard.title: 1 John Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 John Chapter 2.

questions.question: What is the reason John wrote to the recipients of this letter?
options: Because they do not know the truth
To tell them to stop sinning
questions.explanation: John states he has not written because they do not know the truth, but because they do know it. (1 John 2:21)

questions.question: Who is identified as a liar in 1 John 2:22?
options: One who denies Jesus is the Christ
questions.correctAnswer: One who denies Jesus is the Christ
questions.explanation: The verse states that the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ is a liar and is referred to as antichrist. (1 John 2:22)

questions.question: What does 1 John 2:23 indicate about denying the Son?
options: It means one does not have the Father
It is acceptable if done in ignorance
questions.correctAnswer: It means one does not have the Father
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that whoever denies the Son does not have the Father. (1 John 2:23)

questions.question: According to 1 John 2:25, what has God promised us?
questions.explanation: This verse specifically mentions that the promise from God is eternal life. (1 John 2:25)

questions.question: What should abide in the believers according to 1 John 2:24?
options: What they have heard from the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: What they have heard from the beginning
questions.explanation: The verse instructs believers to let what they have heard from the beginning abide in them. (1 John 2:24)

questions.question: What is the nature of the anointing mentioned in 1 John 2:27?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the anointing teaches believers all things and is truth, not a lie. (1 John 2:27)

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'Christos' in 1 John 2:22 mean?
questions.explanation: The word 'Christos' translates to 'Messiah', indicating the anointed one of God. (1 John 2:22)

questions.question: What literary device is used in 1 John 2:28 when it speaks of confidence at His coming?
questions.explanation: The mention of confidence at His coming foreshadows the future return of Christ and the believers' anticipation. (1 John 2:28)

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of 'denying the Son' from 1 John 2:23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:33 states that whoever denies Jesus before men will be denied before the Father, echoing the theme of denial. (1 John 2:23)

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the promise of eternal life mentioned in 1 John 2:25?
questions.explanation: John 3:16 emphasizes eternal life as a promise to those who believe in Jesus, paralleling the promise in 1 John 2:25. (1 John 2:25)

questions.question: What comes before 1 John 2:26?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:25 directly precedes 1 John 2:26, discussing the promise of eternal life. (1 John 2:26)

questions.question: What is the theme of 1 John 2:29 regarding righteousness?
options: Righteousness indicates one is born of God
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness indicates one is born of God
questions.explanation: The verse asserts that knowing He is righteous means that one who does righteousness is born of Him. (1 John 2:29)

questions.question: The statement 'the truth is not in him' refers to which character in 1 John 2:4?
questions.explanation: This phrase describes anyone who claims to know God but does not keep His commandments, referring to the liar. (1 John 2:4)

questions.question: True or False: The anointing mentioned in 1 John 2:27 is a temporary gift.
questions.explanation: The anointing is described as abiding in believers, indicating it is not temporary. (1 John 2:27)

questions.question: True or False: 1 John 2:10 states that he who loves his brother is in darkness.
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:10 states that he who loves his brother abides in the light, not in darkness. (1 John 2:10)

theological.title: 1 John Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 John Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 2:2 teach about the scope of Christ's propitiation in salvation?
options: Christ's propitiation is only for the sins of believers
Christ's propitiation is for the sins of the whole world
Christ's propitiation is limited to the Jewish people
Christ's propitiation is only effective for the elect
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's propitiation is for the sins of the whole world
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:2 explicitly states that Jesus Christ is the propitiation for our sins and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world, indicating the universal scope of His atoning sacrifice.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 2:4 teach about the relationship between claiming to know God and obedience?
options: Knowing God can be genuine without obedience
Claiming to know God without keeping commandments is falsehood
Obedience is optional for true believers
Confession alone guarantees true knowledge of God
questions.correctAnswer: Claiming to know God without keeping commandments is falsehood
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:4 states that he who says 'I know Him' but does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, emphasizing the inseparability of true knowledge of God and obedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in 1 John 2:6 regarding the Christian's conduct?
options: Believers must walk as Jesus walked to abide in Him
Walking as Jesus walked is impossible for believers
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must walk as Jesus walked to abide in Him
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:6 teaches that whoever claims to abide in Christ must also walk in the same manner as Jesus walked, indicating that sanctification involves imitating Christ's example in daily living.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 2:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:1 presents Jesus Christ as an advocate with the Father for sinners, demonstrating the divine attribute of advocacy on behalf of humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 2:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:25 refers to the promise of eternal life that God has promised us, demonstrating God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises.

questions.question: How does 1 John 2:18 connect to the wider biblical theme of eschatology?
options: It denies the coming of antichrists
It declares the 'last time' and the presence of many antichrists
It focuses solely on Christ's first coming
It teaches that antichrists will never appear
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the 'last time' and the presence of many antichrists
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:18 identifies the current period as 'the last time' and notes the presence of many antichrists, linking this chapter to New Testament eschatological teachings about the end times and false teachers.

questions.question: In what way does 1 John 2:22-23 prepare for Christological confession in the New Testament?
options: By denying the necessity of confessing Jesus as Christ
By equating denial of Jesus as Christ with being antichrist
questions.correctAnswer: By equating denial of Jesus as Christ with being antichrist
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:22-23 teaches that whoever denies Jesus is the Christ is a liar and the antichrist, preparing the church for orthodox Christological confession foundational in the New Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 John 2:15 and 1 John 2:16 teach about Christian affections and the world?
options: Loving the world is consistent with loving the Father
The lust of the flesh, eyes, and pride of life are from the Father
Loving the world excludes the love of the Father because worldly lusts are not of God
The world is neutral in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: Loving the world excludes the love of the Father because worldly lusts are not of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:15-16 teaches that love for the world and its lusts are contrary to the love of the Father, emphasizing the theological tension between worldly affections and divine love.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 John 2:3 and 1 John 2:5 teach about the evidence of knowing God?
options: Knowing God is proven by verbal confession alone
Keeping commandments and keeping His word perfect the love of God in a believer
Knowledge of God requires no change in behavior
Obedience is irrelevant to knowing God
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping commandments and keeping His word perfect the love of God in a believer
questions.explanation: Verses 1 John 2:3 and 2:5 together indicate that knowing God is evidenced by obedience to His commandments and His word, which perfects the love of God in a person.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 John 2:26-27 teach about the believer's protection against deception?
options: Believers rely solely on human teachers for truth
The anointing from the Holy One teaches all things and guards against seduction
The anointing is a temporary gift
questions.correctAnswer: The anointing from the Holy One teaches all things and guards against seduction
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:26-27 teaches that the anointing believers receive from the Holy One abides in them, teaching them all things and protecting them from deception by false teachers.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 John 2:19 teaches that those who leave the church were never true believers. What does 1 John 2:19 actually teach?
options: Those who leave were true believers who lost salvation
Those who leave were never genuinely part of the community of faith
Everyone who leaves the church will be saved anyway
Leaving the church has no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Those who leave were never genuinely part of the community of faith
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:19 explains that those who went out from the community were not truly of them, for if they had been, they would have continued, indicating they were never genuine believers.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 2:29 teach about the relationship between righteousness and regeneration?
options: Doing righteousness proves one is born of God
Righteousness is unrelated to being born of God
One can be born of God without righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Doing righteousness proves one is born of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:29 teaches that everyone who does righteousness is born of God, linking righteous conduct as evidence of regeneration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 John 2:20 by the believer's reception of an unction from the Holy One?
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:20 states believers have an unction from the Holy One and know all things, demonstrating God's attribute of illumination by the Spirit.

questions.question: What theological theme is advanced by 1 John 2:7–8 regarding the old and new commandments?
options: The new commandment replaces the old completely
The new commandment is actually a fulfillment and continuation of the old
The old commandment is obsolete and irrelevant
The new commandment contradicts the old
questions.correctAnswer: The new commandment is actually a fulfillment and continuation of the old
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:7-8 explains that the commandment written is old and known from the beginning but also a new commandment true in Christ and believers, indicating continuity and fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 2:10 and 1 John 2:11 teach about love and spiritual condition?
options: Hatred is consistent with walking in the light
Love for one's brother indicates abiding in the light and prevents stumbling
Love is unrelated to spiritual condition
Walking in darkness is a sign of spiritual maturity
questions.correctAnswer: Love for one's brother indicates abiding in the light and prevents stumbling
questions.explanation: 1 John 2:10-11 links love for the brother with abiding in the light and absence of stumbling, while hatred is associated with darkness and blindness.
